sections.h2: Where is the McDowell County, NC Register of Deeds and what does it do?
sections.html:
The office is at 35 West Fort Street in Marion, and the county lists hours of Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 5:00pm. The phone is 828-652-4727. The county's website points to McDowellDeeds.com for online services.

By the county's own description, the office records, indexes and stores real estate and business documents presented for recording. It also issues marriage licenses, gives notary oaths, records notary commissions, helps veterans record discharge records and provides certified copies, including birth and death records.

For a home seller, the land records are the part that counts. A deed, a deed of trust and a lien release all pass through this counter, and the registrar's stated mission is the integrity, completeness, accuracy and safekeeping of the public record.

sections.h2: Can McDowell County documents be recorded electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. The county says all documents can be electronically recorded, and it lists three providers, so a closing attorney in another city does not need to send a runner to Marion.

Your attorney or title company picks the vendor, not you. If you sign a deed in a different state, ask whether the notary acknowledgment is in a form the register of deeds will accept before the originals go in the mail. Paper recording still works at the counter.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in McDowell County?
sections.html:
McDowell County charges the uniform state fees, which G.S. 161-10 sets for every county. A deed or other instrument is $26.00 for the first 15 pages plus $4.00 for each additional page, and a deed of trust or mortgage is $64.00 for the first 35 pages plus $4.00 for each additional page.

  • No fee for recording a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust.
  • Plats are $21.00 per sheet.
  • A certified copy is $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each additional page.
  • A nonstandard document adds $25.00.
  • Each additional instrument in one document adds $10.00.

The statute describes these fees as complete and exclusive and says they are collected before the document is filed. Call 828-652-4727 if you want the office to confirm the total for a long document with many exhibits.

sections.h2: How much is the deed transfer tax in McDowell County?
sections.html:
The seller owes $1.00 for each $500 of the price or value of the interest conveyed, counting any remainder under $500 as a full unit. This is the state excise tax in G.S. 105-228.30, and the register of deeds collects it before the instrument goes into the record.

One half goes to the county general fund. The other half, less refunds and the county's allowance, goes to the Department of Revenue each month.

McDowell County's tax foreclosure auctions are a separate matter, and a person buying at one will see the same recording fees and excise rules apply to the deed that follows. For a regular sale, the settlement statement shows the exact transfer tax on the seller's side.

sections.h2: What does McDowell County say about tax foreclosure sales?
sections.html:
McDowell County runs judicial tax foreclosures under G.S. 105-374 and holds its auctions at the McDowell County Courthouse at 21 S. Main St. in Marion. The high bidder must give the commissioner a $1,000.00 cash deposit as soon as the sale ends.

A 10-day upset bid period follows, handled in the Clerk of Court's office. An upset bid must exceed the last highest bid by at least 5 percent, with a minimum increase of $750.00, and every new bid restarts the 10 days. The county's page lists the clerk's number as (828) 655-4100.

  • Active or pending foreclosures are listed on a link on the county's foreclosure page.
  • Parcel details such as map, assessed value, acreage and deed reference come from the county GIS by parcel number.
  • The county tells buyers to research the property themselves, including questions about septic and wells.

If you owe back taxes on a McDowell County house, selling before the auction can leave you with the equity that a sale at the courthouse door would cut into.

sections.h2: Why does recording order matter on a McDowell County sale?
sections.html:
Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance does not bind lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies. For McDowell County land, that is the Marion office, whatever the seller's address.

Priority follows the order in which instruments are registered. A closing attorney therefore records the deed and the buyer's new deed of trust together and in the right sequence, and lender releases go in so old liens come off the record.

If you sell and the title search turns up a lien that was never cancelled, the fix is usually a release from the old lender. Ask your attorney to request it early, because cancellations carry no recording fee but depend on the lender's response time.

sections.h2: What does a McDowell County seller need to know about the local market?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate for McDowell County is 45,198 people, and the 2020 count was 44,578. The county has 22,036 housing units and 18,638 households for 2020 to 2024, with an owner-occupied rate of 75.6 percent.

The median value of an owner-occupied home was $171,100 and median gross rent was $806 for 2020 to 2024. Median household income was $57,168 in 2024 dollars. The county had 164 building permits in 2025, and 2,760 veterans live there, which matters because disabled veterans can qualify for a property tax exclusion.

Land area is 439.95 square miles, or about 101 people per square mile in 2020. With most homes owner-occupied and many older houses, probate sales, inherited property and homes needing repair are common reasons for a cash sale. Ask the tax collector at (828) 652-0701 for a payoff figure, and have the register of deeds confirm the recorded owner before you sign.

faqs.a: Yes. The county states that all documents can be electronically recorded and names three providers: Simplifile, Electronic Document Logistics (EDL) and Corporation Service Company (CSC). Your closing attorney chooses one.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a McDowell County house sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. State law sets the excise tax at $1.00 for each $500 of the price or fraction of $500, and the register of deeds collects it before recording the deed.

faqs.q: How do upset bids work at a McDowell County tax foreclosure sale?
faqs.a: Each upset bid must beat the last bid by at least 5 percent and no less than $750.00. It is filed with the Clerk of Court, and every new bid restarts a 10-day period.
